changelog: ONT WGS customer package + read-based taxonomy + TYGS dDDH + Download results for every pipeline. (1) ONT WGS: per sample a package laid out like the lab's: folders 1.QcReads, 2.Assembly, 3.Completeness, 4.Taxonomy (TYGS, Read-based Taxonomy, Contig-based Taxonomy, 16S, MLST, Phylogeny), 5.ANI, 6.Annotation, 7.AMR (AMRFinderPlus, VFDB, PlasmidFinder, MOB-suite), 8.readsMappingToRef, and Report_<sample>.pdf / .docx ('Whole genome sequencing report', no cover, each section ending 'Results <folder>'); only steps that ran and only our tools are named. (2) Read-based taxonomy (new WGS step, also 'Add read-based taxonomy' on a finished job through the queue): Kraken2+Bracken (existing Kraken2 DB), Centrifuger (RefSeq 2023 index; Centrifuge p+h+v when WSL has < 60 GB RAM) and GOTTCHA2 2.5 nanopore mode (RefSeq-GTDB multi-domain+ fast DB) on the filtered reads; heatmap in the report; a missing tool or DB = one column less with a note. Install: bash setup_wgs.sh --readtax --db-dir /mnt/e/ngamp-db/readtax (refuses a download that would leave < 20 GB free). (3) dDDH from TYGS: Genome report → 'Assembly for TYGS', upload it yourself at tygs.dsmz.de (the genome goes to DSMZ), paste the result link → Import: Table 4.1, the dDDH table (d0/d4/d6) and the TYGS trees; other genomes of the same TYGS job are left out; an unfinished TYGS job is re-checked at most every 30 min. (4) Download results (Job Detail, all pipelines): tick samples (filter box for long runs), one zip per sample (default) or one zip. One standard for every pipeline: numbered folders + Report_<sample>.pdf/.docx laid out like the WGS report (no cover, numbered sections, each ending 'Results <folder>'). Amplicon (ONT 16S, 16S, 12S/CytB): 1.QcReads (read tracking, NanoPlot or FastQC/fastp, DADA2 quality profiles, filtered reads optional), 2.Taxonomy (tables per rank, ASV FASTA, BIOM, bar charts, Top 50 heatmap, Krona, Emu's own table, BLAST/NCBI check), 3.Diversity (alpha, rarefaction), 4.Tables (Excel); a step that did not run leaves NOT_AVAILABLE.txt; built through the job queue with progress, zips written to disk (results/<job>/packages). 'Everything (.zip)' is now written to disk instead of memory. Backend restart required.

previous.changelog: fix: Customer report Top 50 heatmap (microbiomeutilities): rows read 'SV001:Brevundimonas sp. DS20' instead of the taxon name printed twice. Backend restart required.

fix: (1) Customer report (ONT 16S): read quality given two ways — over whole reads, and without the first 60 bases, the way MinKNOW scores a read (so it can be compared with the MinKNOW report). (2) Top 50 heatmap: microbiomeutilities is called without column clustering (one sample per report), so it no longer falls back to pheatmap. (3) The R figure log is kept beside each package (<sample>_customer_report.plots.log) for checking. Backend restart required.

fix: (1) Customer report (ONT 16S): mean read quality is now computed from each read's mean error rate, as MinKNOW and NanoPlot do — the mean of the Phred numbers overstated it (Q38.6 instead of about Q21.7). Rebuild a customer report made with 2.24.0 to get the right value. (2) setup_amplicon_report.sh installs gghalves (GitHub) and Bioconductor microbiome before microbiomeutilities, and says when venneuler needs Java. Backend restart required.

Customer report per sample. (1) Job Detail → Build report → Customer report: tick the samples and pick 'One report per sample' (default) or 'One report for the chosen samples'. Per sample = one zip (<sample>_customer_report.zip: Word + PDF, R figures, tables, Excel, BIOM, FASTA, filtered reads) built from a view of the run holding only that sample — no name, taxon, count or figure of another sample, NCBI counts and SV numbers recomputed for it; for runs whose samples belong to different customers. (2) The customer report now covers 16S Illumina (DADA2) and ONT 16S (Emu) as well as 12S / CytB, each with its real methods: ONT = read statistics (+ NanoPlot when installed), Chopper Q / length filter, cutadapt primer removal, Emu with its database and minimum abundance. (3) emu_pipeline.py records its QC / trimming settings in summary.json. Install NanoPlot (optional): bash setup_amplicon_report.sh. (4) Job queue: one job at a time by default and a 3-minute pause after each job ends (finished, failed or cancelled) before the next starts — both in Settings and saved across restarts. New Queue page: what runs, the pause countdown, the waiting jobs in order with ↑ / ↓ / To front / Cancel; the order is saved. Jobs still waiting when the backend restarts go back in the queue in their order (after one pause) instead of failing. Changing 'Jobs at once' while jobs wait no longer lets more jobs run than set. Backend restart required.

12S / CytB fish eDNA. (1) CytB: preset 'CytB fish (L14912 / H15149)' on the 12S / CytB pipeline (12S licence), MIDORI2 CytB trainset. (2) Species names by BLASTn (12S/CytB, on by default for new 12S runs; DADA2 kept beside): reference built from the newest MIDORI2 (GenBank, Leray et al. 2022) + newest MitoFish (Zhu et al. 2023), with records MitoFish judges mislabelled (heterospecific) and records with >1% ambiguous bases removed; limited to fish (NCBI: txid 7898 ray-finned + txid 7777 cartilaginous) or vertebrates (txid 7742); a sequence filed under several species is kept once and named to their shared rank; up to 5000 hits per ASV so ties are never cut off; lowest common rank of ties within 0.5%, never a species below 98.5% (genus 95, family 90, order 85, class 80); human and other non-target ASVs keep their real names; every ASV checked against NCBI nt (BLAST URL API), disagreements and NCBI species ties cut to the shared rank and flagged; a failed NCBI batch keeps the finished ones (its ASVs: not checked). Install: bash download_databases.sh --fishmito. (3) Customer report (Job Detail → Build report → Customer report): the lab's per-sample format, same headings and figure placement, cover left blank for the BI team, no company name; Word + PDF + SampleN_ folders (Box plot, bar charts per rank, Top 50 heatmap, Krona, rarefaction, alpha, outfiles, BIOM, Excel per sample) as one zip; FastQC, fastp, cutadapt, DADA2, BLASTn, phyloseq, ggplot2, microbiomeutilities, Krona, vegan. Install: bash setup_amplicon_report.sh. The report states only what the run did (pool, rm.phix, fastp as a check, BLAST skipped, unknown raw counts, samples the pipeline dropped). Backend restart required.

setup_shotgun.sh --func: the conda env ngamp-func was created with python 3.10, but bioconda builds humann 3.9 for python 3.12 only, so 'humann_databases' stopped with "No module named 'humann'". The env now uses python 3.12, is checked by importing humann and metaphlan, and a broken env is rebuilt. Nothing else changes; no backend restart needed.
